mainEntity.name: Can a Conveyor System Be Customized to My Exact Plant Layout?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. TRFIntraflow is custom-engineered around each plant's production flow, layout and operational requirements, using standard modules for straight conveying, curves and transfers, accumulation, merging, diverting, sorting and elevation. TRF takes the project from concept and engineering to manufacturing, controls, installation and commissioning, so the layout fits your hall.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between a Merge, a Divert and a Sorting Conveyor?

acceptedAnswer.text: A merge combines units from several lines into one lane, a divert moves units from one lane to another, and a sorting conveyor sends each unit to its destination based on identification such as a barcode. In converting plants, these modules route each order to the right palletizer or staging lane. TRFIntraflow includes all three.

mainEntity.name: How Many Cases per Minute Can a Robotic Palletizer Handle?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the platform. TRFCobot covers about 1 to 10 cases per minute, TRFCompact about 5 to 15 and TRFSpeed about 10 to 35. These are typical ranges for commercial screening: TRF confirms the final rate for your units, end-of-arm tool, pallet pattern and reach.

mainEntity.name: Can a Palletizer Be Integrated With My Existing Conveyor and Wrapping Line?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. TRFIntraflow supplies the accumulation, machine communication and palletizer interfaces that connect a new cell to the conveyors already installed, and TRFSpeed projects can include interfaces to wrapping, labeling and warehouse systems. Each interface with your converting and shipping equipment is defined during project engineering, so one partner owns the result.

mainEntity.name: How Is Payback Estimated for a Robotic Palletizer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Payback depends on the labor hours the palletizer replaces, shifts per day, local labor cost and the installed cost of the system. The estimate follows the method of the A3 (Association for Advancing Automation) robot ROI calculator: the system cost, including 20 years of maintenance at 5% per year, divided by the annual net savings, which is the labor cost of manual palletizing minus the electricity the robot uses. Converting plants should also count order changeover time.
